utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. And we hope that all of us will get used to the new courtroom layout before too long. At the moment it feels quite unusual, I think, for most people. May I remind you, sir, of the affirmation at the beginning of your evidence, which still applies. Now, Mr. Vasic, you were questioning.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Good afternoon Your Honours, good afternoon to everyone in the courtroom. Mr. Kypr, good afternoon. First of all, I would like to do something that is still open after yesterday's session, and that is to give the number for Exhibit 324. Yesterday it was 0D05-0213. Now we have all the references for this exhibit, I think. Thank you. Mr. Kypr, yesterday at the end of the session we talked about the events relating to the Ilok area, and then later the Brsadin village area. First of all, I would like to ask you if you remember that on the 15th of October, 1991 you were in a monitoring mission delegation that visited Ilok and which comprised Mr. Cunningham, Mr. Waters, Mr. Finakaliotis and yourself. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that. I don't have it in my memory, but we can check it in the evidences.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we now look at document bearing the number 0D00-0912. That's the B/C/S version, and then the English version is attached, 0D00-0915. That is a report of the commission monitoring the implementation of the cease-fire and also monitoring the activities of the European Monitoring Mission which was sent to the operative centre of the armed forces of the SFRY.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, sir. I can't read it. It's too small.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is this better now? Could we now maybe focus on the bottom part of this page? Thank you. Mr. Kypr, could we please look at this first passage and could you please confirm if you remember what it says. In item 2, it says, "The activities of the European Community Monitoring Mission."

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can read it, but the document isn't -- isn't mine or -- or I -- I haven't seen it before.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Yes, I know that it's not your document. I am going to provide you with the following reference of your document. Mr. Kypr, I don't have the document written by your mission on the 13th of October. Obviously the document is somewhere in the archives of the European Monitoring Mission, which we have not obtained. But we will try to go through the document of the Monitoring Commission, and perhaps you can remember the events that took place at the time. In paragraph 2 it states that: "On the bridge 25th of May, at 10.00 they were received by the commander of the unit, Colonel Grahovac," and he talks about the European Mission. Transcript, page 2, line 22: It's the bridge named the 25th of May. And briefly, he acquainted them with the measures and activities in the course of the day in relation to yesterday's agreement. And the commander stressed that in the course of the previous night there were armed conflict between different factions in Ilok. The meeting was covered by a crew from TV Belgrade. In the course of the day the mission intensively worked to establish and implement the duties arising from the agreement.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters note we don't know where the counsel is reading from.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: At 1600 hours the approaches to Ilok were de-mined and a unit of the JNA left to check this together with the monitors. Also, according to our information --

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no text on my display. The new text.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: You are right. I apologise. Can we move to page 2 now. Could you please enlarge or zoom in on the first two paragraphs. I'm going to repeat: "At approximately 1600 hours, according to the information that we have, the road around Ilok was de-mined and a JNA unit left to check that, together with the observers, or the monitors. Also, according to our information, a large quantity of weapons has been returned in the following places: Mohovo, Sarengrad and Bapska." Do you remember being together with Colonel Grahovac during the preparations for the signing of the agreement and that you went to inspect the area around Ilok that was de-mined? Please wait until the end of the translation.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... teams of the ECMM have met a few times Colonel Grahovac, but I don't know the -- if the date is -- is right, and so I cannot confirm that this document is -- is valid or not. And I -- I -- it didn't help me to -- to refresh my memory. But we were working there in Ilok many times because we felt that it's very important, and so we sent them there, teams, almost each day.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Does that mean that almost every day a team of the Monitoring Mission was in Ilok in that period from mid-October until late October, 1991?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... sorry, excuse me, please. I assume that it was all -- each -- each day or that the period was maximally three days.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to tender this document as an exhibit for the activities of the European Monitoring Mission in the area of Ilok.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit Number 325.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kypr, could you please turn to tab 18, please.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We have a report here by the European Monitoring Mission team. Were you a part of that team? Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that I was not there, because I am not mentioned in the first part of the table.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. It's a document in tab 18, and it's number 00381383, and the B/C/S translation is 0304040700. Could you please read what it states in paragraph 3, and can you please tell us if you know about the contents.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: While the witness is looking for that section, I just want to say that this document is number 0D05-0187. That's the original, and 0D050-819 for the B/C/S. So the original has the number 0D05-0187, and the B/C/S version 0D05-0189. Mr. Kypr, have you managed to find the document? That's why I did mention that it was in tab 18.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Your Honour, I do have a question. I don't remember the situation there, but I have a copy of my notebook, the other notebook from the previous time that was displayed before, and there are some written remarks about the 19th of October. May I use it as a -- as the answer, or ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think we take this in stages. First you say you don't know of the report. And does this mean that you can't verify anything about its contents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't remember the -- the -- the meeting there, but I know that the -- some Croatian representatives came over the front line to see the situation in Ilok. And I know, I remember that I was in the team of ECMM which crossed over the -- the front line to pick up the delegation and to bring them to Ilok. The way back was covered by another team, so I don't remember the -- the -- the last part of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Are you able to say when that was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't remember exact date if I am not using papers, so according my memory, I know that it was one or two days after surrender of Ilok.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Are you able to say whether Colonel Grahovac was one of the JNA representatives who met those Croatian people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I -- I can only try to think about that, but -- but I have no real memory about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Vasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Perhaps we can try it in this way: I would like to ask the witness whether this report, which is in tab 18 that we're just looking at, did you obtain a copy of that report from the archives of the regional centre of the European Monitoring Mission and hand it over to Mr. Vladimir Dzuro, the investigator of the ICTY?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please wait for the translation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Kypr, you answer very quickly and before the translators are finished with the question. If you can remember to try and pause. Thank you. Do you wish to tender the report, Mr. Vasic?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 326, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Could we now look at document 0D00-0183 on the screen. That's the B/C/S version. The English version is 0D00-0186. That's a report of the commission monitoring the activities of the Monitoring Mission sent to the Main Staff of the SFRY armed forces on the 19th of October, 1991, and which deals with the topic from the document that we tendered a little bit earlier. Could we look at the bottom of the page, please. Thank you very much. Item 2, it says "Activities of the European Community Monitoring Mission," and it says: "The three-member EC Monitoring Mission at 7.30 hours set off from Avala with the aim of monitoring the situation relating to the convoy --" and then it's, "(Doctors Without Borders) in order to pull out the wounded from Vukovar. However, once they passed Tovarnik (on the way to Vukovar) they were informed by their centre in Zagreb to return to the motorway and wait for a delegation of the Croatian Sabor Assembly and to travel to Ilok." Mr. Kypr, did you -- were you amongst those members of that team that went together to monitor the situation with this convoy and that was told to return? Earlier you told us that you went through the front line and you brought the observers with you and that you then handed them over to another observer team; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: This document from which I read the first paragraph bears the date 19th of October, 1991, as well as the document which was drafted by the Monitoring Mission, a document that we tendered previously. That is why I'm asking you, were you in that part of the delegation which just escorted these people from the Croatian Assembly to Ilok and then you handed them over to another team; is that clear from this paragraph that we have just read?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I assume that, yes, but I cannot tell even if there are two delegations in various times, so I really don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Kypr, I would just like you to wait after my question. I'm going to make a pause after your question [as interpreted], so that the interpreters can complete their translation.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: It's for the purposes of the transcript because if two speakers speaking English speak at the same time, the court reporter can only write down what one speaker is saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to tender this document as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit Number 327.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kypr, I would like you to turn to tab 16, please. This is document 0D05-0067. That's the original. And the B/C/S translation is 0D05-0069. Have you found this document, Mr. Kypr?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you kindly read the first and the second paragraph of this document, what it states below the words, "Ilok evacuation." And if you can read slowly so that the interpreters can interpret it.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The evacuation was originally intended to start at 0700 hours the 17th of October, 1991, with the handover of weapons by the village --" I don't know the abbreviation -- "to the JNA," probably. "The weaponry handover was delayed to approximately 0930. The formal --" I'm not quite sure about the word -- "evacuation started at approximately 1000 hours. The JNA reported that 3.368 people, (plus minus) and 536 vehicles (plus minus) departed Ilok for various destinations." Point 2: "The conduct of the JNA during the evacuation was beyond --" I'm sorry, I can't read it. "The evacuation was --" it's illegible for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kypr --

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The evacuation was carried out in a professional --" it's illegible for me -- "manner at all times. JNA soldiers assisted --" I can't read it. Illegible, "people with their belongings to the point of carrying bags and pushing stalled vehicles. One lady, due to give birth, was expedited through the check-point with stated that he and other Serbs --" sorry, there is no sense. There is something missing in between.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In the translation I have, the text does not end on this page, as you can see for yourself. Is this a document that you received from the archives of the regional centre of the ECMM?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: According the signature and symbols there, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The document we can see on the screen is a different one, hence I wanted to repeat the number. Now we have the right one. Now we have the right one.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I beg your pardon, the mistake is all mine because I invoked a document from another package, but now we have the right document on the screen. I apologise, but we have so many references, so many documents, that mistakes do happen. Hence, the correct number is 0D05-0180 for the original, and in B/C/S 0D05-0182. I would like to tender this document, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Vasic, do you want the transcript to reflect what was being read? As we appreciate, Mr. Kypr has had recent eye surgery and he cannot read very well, he explained. So he's missed a lot. What was read out from paragraph 2 was: "The conduct of the JNA during the evacuation was beyond reproach. The evacuation was carried out in a professional, courteous manner at all times. JNA soldiers assisted elderly people with their belongings to the point of carrying bags and pushing stalled vehicles. One lady, due to give birth, was expedited through the check-points with --" and then, as the witness said, there's some lack of coherence in the sentence -- "with stated that he and other Serb volunteers had attacked specific houses in Lovas 10 October, 1991 to 'prevent' Serbs from being slaughtered - during the attack 22 Croats and one Serb were killed." I think that's beyond the point you were wanting read. Could I observe that it appears to me that the continuation page is dealing with an entirely different subject from the first page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir, you are right. Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And you will notice, as has been pointed out to me by Judge Thelin, that on the second page there is a paragraph numbered 2 which says, "For your info," or information, whereas on the first page what I was reading is numbered paragraph 2. So I think we have two different documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. You are completely right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: I wanted to ask Mr. Kypr for a clarification. Do you believe, Mr. Kypr, that these are two separate documents that we can see on the two pages?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. As far as I can see, the other document we mentioned pertains to Lovas and the first document pertains to Ilok.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: If it helps my learned friend and the Court, if you look at tab 13 and look at tab 16, you will find in actual fact what I will call the second page is the same page, and it also seems to be that in tab 13 it flows logically. "He also stated ..." whereas tab 16 it is -- it does not flow. So it would appear that the tab 13 document is correct with regard to the second page, whereas the tab 16 second page is incorrect.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to thank my learned friend for the clarification. He is obviously right. Since the entire first page had been read out, of this document, I don't think there is any need to tender the document itself, as its contents have been entered into the transcript. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kypr, do you know whether members of the ECMM during the 29th -- that is, the 28th, the 29th and the 30th of October of 1991 met with representatives of the JNA as well as the representatives of the government of Eastern Slavonia, Western Srem and Baranja in a place called Tenja close to Osijek. Are you familiar with that?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: I will try to refresh your memory. I would kindly ask that document 0D00-0167 in B/C/S be put on the screen. And in English it's 0D00-0169. Again, it is a report of the aforementioned commission, monitoring the activities of European monitors. The date is the 30th of September, 1991. Thank you. Could we please zoom in on the second part. Thank you. In item 2, it says: "Activities of the Monitoring Mission. During the 29th of September, 1991 in the area of the Tenja military facility a meeting was held between members of the peacekeeping mission of the European Commission with the representatives of the JNA (Colonel Adam Loncar, Colonel Vujica Rakicevic and Colonel Boro Ivanovic) and on behalf of the SAO Slavonia, Baranja and Western Srem, the two ministers of the government attended, namely Rada Leskovac and Slobodan Rajic." For the transcript: Rade Leskovac and Slobodan Rajic. Another correction for the transcript: Page 20, line 22. The name is Rade, R-a-d-e, masculine. Mr. Kypr, sir, are you familiar with such a meeting involving the people I've -- whose names I've read?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... territory and that I was a member of the team, but I -- I don't remember more.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you remember whether during those discussions you were given a report on the situation of detention facilities in Osijek; that is, members of the JNA who were imprisoned in Osijek? Could we please go to page 2 of this document. Is this topic familiar to you?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have been with one team in Osijek in the prison, and I was a member of the team. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this document, Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit Number 328.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Your Honour, before we proceed, I'm sorry. Could I just clarify, in relation to the documents that my learned friend is putting in, certainly Ambassador Kypr is accepting that -- that he was a member of the mission, but to what do the documents go upon -- to what issue are the Defence relying upon if the document is flowing from -- from the ambassador? He said he was there, but he has been asked no other questions about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Moore, that could be an issue to be dealt with in final address.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Well, I certainly will try, but all I really wish is for clarification, because there's been no questions about the mission itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Whether the document is being put in testimonially.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It is at the moment. It is being put in on the basis that it's a document, as with your documents, that were identified by the witness either as coming from a report of the ECMM --

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: -- or, in this case, as a document, it would appear, of the JNA, dealing with the same topic. Now, if you like, we can air the issue now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Well, I don't wish to air it extensively. Might I just try and, for clarification, the documents that we have put in have been ECMM documents of -- this is a witness who worked for the ECMM at that time, and they're put in testimonially and he was asked about the content of the documents, sometimes he didn't know, other times he did. In my submission, the distinction that can be drawn here is that this is a witness who cannot attest to the authenticity of these documents, but merely the fact that a mission had occurred. That's where the distinction would be, I would submit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That, I believe, has become clear in the question that is asked of him. The point of this, Mr. Vasic, of course, is that Mr. Moore is saying this witness has not said anything about the truth of what is in this report. He says he doesn't know about it. He can tell you, perhaps, that he was part of an ECMM mission that was referred to in this report, but he can't tell you whether anything set out in the report is correct or not. So perhaps to avoid misconception, Mr. Moore is flagging the point now so that you realise this document doesn't prove the truth of what's set out in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I asked the witness first about the documents themselves, that is of the Monitoring Commission, the activities of the ECMM. And yesterday he replied that he had no knowledge of such reports, and today with each of the reports I asked him about a specific event described in a given report. From our esteemed colleague Mr. Moore and the witness, we received the reports of the ECMM. He was a member of the mission, but as concerns most of these reports, he had no part in their drafting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Vasic, we are not dealing specifically with the ECMM reports. We are dealing with the reports such as the one you have just tendered, which is not an ECMM report. This witness knows nothing of the report. He says that the only thing he can say about it is that he was a member of an ECMM mission that was referred to in one place in the report. It appears to be a report from the First Military District of the JNA to the General Staff. Now, this is evidence that you tender, but be aware that there is nothing in the -- what the witness has said that can verify anything about the truth of what is in there except that there was an ECMM mission. Everything else is not being proved by this document. Mr. Moore is just wanting, as a matter of caution, for you to be clear of that now rather than think that you have now proved everything that's in this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I completely understand Mr. Moore's position. I asked the witness some questions in relation to portions of these documents. For example, the discussion concerning the imprisoned JNA members in Osijek. He participated in those, and he confirmed that. As regards the remaining portion of the document that the witness cannot speak about, the Defence will call witnesses who will be able to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think I have unnecessarily delayed, but Mr. Moore raised the point. I wanted to make clear, in my mind, that were you aware. I think the position is clear to everybody. Thank you, Mr. Vasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Vasic. You have mentioned prisons as a plural. I remember that we have been on -- only in one prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: No, Mr. Kypr, I didn't say prisons, I mentioned the prison in Osijek, but I did mention that there were several people detained. Thank you in any case. Did you know that on the 11th of October, 1991 -- or to say at the beginning of October, a liaison officer from your mission came to your headquarters at Avala in order to speak with the mission representatives and with Mr. Michel Perrin regarding the passage of convoy with medication, supplies --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters apologise, but did not manage to hear the route of the convoy.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that at the beginning of October you were notified by one of your liaison officers that in Sarengrad there was a crime committed against the Serb civilian population immediately after the mission left the locality. Do you remember that? And because of that, Mr. Perrin expressed his views relating to the events.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge of Croatian armed forces setting four houses aflame and that they slaughtered the people who lived in them in October, 1991?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, sir. Maybe it would be useful if I explain the position, my position within the mission. Then you can understand better why I -- I am not aware of many things.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was there as a -- not only as a monitor on the front line, but when we came back from the mission, in the evening I have to go through media, Serb media, means watch TV, to go through press, to see messages from Croatia on Croatian, and try to explain it to -- to my colleagues to be aware of the situation in society we are living, or we are facing with. So it was really demanding and then I had no so much time to follow all those situations. Sometimes I -- I was not present in -- in debriefings of teams. So it's only for your knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kypr, sir. Do you have any knowledge about the convoy that had left on the 11th of October from Vinkovci towards Vukovar, and it was a humanitarian convoy. Did you know that an explosive device was found on one of the trucks amongst the supplies, the food, and then the convoy was returned from Nustar to Vinkovci, and then in their second attempt, on the 13th of October, it finally managed to reach the Vukovar barracks?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that from Serb media.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Were you present when a person by the name of Davro Mihaljevic, on the 18th of October, 1991 - and by the way, this person was the driver of the truck on board which the device was found, and he was arrested - on that day he was handed over to the members of the ECMM in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I do remember that there was some Croat given to our hands, and he was sleeping there in the -- in the -- one of the rooms of the mission's hotel. But I don't know anything about his next destiny or -- or...

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we now please see document 0D00-0179 in the original, put on the screen, as well as 0D00-0181 in English. Thank you very much. Could we zoom in on the bottom part of the document. Thank you. Mr. Kypr, under 2, where it states, "Activities of the European Community Monitor Mission," it states: "In the course of the day the observer mission of the European Community did not have any activities in the area of the First Military District today, owing to mediation by the mission, Davro Mihaljevic, a soldier born on the 14th of October, 1963 in Vukovar was released from prison and turned over to the mission today. He was brought in on the 11th of October, 1991, after a bomb was found in his vehicle in a convoy with food for Vukovar." Then it goes on to say: "He was released on order and turned over to the mission at Avala at 10.50 hours where he stated in writing: 'From the moment I was brought in I was -- on October 11th, 1991, I was not mistreated or injured in any manner by the JNA or by anyone else and I do not think I need a medical examination.'" Is this the event or an event that you were present at and that you talked about?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... only what I already have said, that there was one Croat hand over to our hands, but I cannot confirm that the date is right or -- or that the -- the declaration made there is -- is authentic. Maybe I can stress, if I can see the -- the other -- the next sentence, I saw parts from those documents published in daily press bulletin or press release of JNA, and it was really for -- for PR. And there, in the second sentence, you can see how it worked that "humanitarian convoy" is in quotation marks to show that it is probably not humanitarian, or not convoy. So it -- I -- I would like only to show in which environment we were working. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to tender this document as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit Number 329.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Kypr, were you in the Monitoring Mission that came to the Vukovar barracks with the convoy on the 13th of October, 1991? Do you have any information about that?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Were you in any humanitarian convoy that came to Vukovar in October with -- from the Croatian side?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... according to my knowledge, Dr. Schou was there. But not me. The convoy went from Croatian side, you told me, and we were serving on -- on -- in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: And did Dr. Schou also serve in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: In October, 1991, where did he serve?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether he was in Belgrade at the time, or you don't recall that either?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you hear from any Ilok citizens whether there was a terrorist attack conducted that was thwarted by the police, the attack was supposed to be have been carried out by the Croatian terrorists?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could we now look at Exhibit 313 on our screens. Mr. Kypr, that is tab 19. Could we look at page 03040396 in B/C/S, and in English it would be page 00381386. Mr. Kypr, look at this report. Father Markos is mentioned in it. Can you please tell us whether this is a Catholic priest or not. Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. What I know is that there was some monastery in Ilok and Catholic church, but I can't say if it is an Orthodox or Catholic priest, Markos, because it is not my report, and I was not there, I believe. According those members of teams, you can see that it is -- there are two teams, but not -- not me.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: What I would like to know is whether, during the time that you went to Ilok, did you meet Father Markos? And that's why I wanted to ask you whether he was a priest of the Franciscan order or not.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... that we were speaking about -- about the situation during the evacuation and problems with -- with things there in the church.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We continue, Mr. Kypr, to miss the first part of your answers. I know it's natural to respond immediately to the question, but if you could try to pause. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kypr, would you be kind enough to repeat the whole answer, and wait until I finish, and then after, make a little pause and then begin.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. I remember that I was in the Catholic church and I was speaking with the priest. Not only me, the -- the whole team. And we were speaking about problems during the possible evacuation.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you talk with these priests sometime after the evacuation as well?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember if I was there, but I remember that there was some report afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Do you remember whether the report said that people were slowly returning to Ilok?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember, sir. But I remember the information from my ambassador, means Czechoslovak ambassador, that Slovaks who remained there, who decided to stay there, had certain problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: I would like you then, please, to read what it states in one of the paragraphs of this report that you have in front of you. 10.30, arrival at Ilok. What did the observer mission note down in that first paragraph?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Meeting at the JNA headquarters with Lieutenant Colonel Lazic Radisa, and Lieutenant Egic Zdravko (German translate). The priest Father Markos arrived after 15 minutes. Situation in Ilok is quiet. Some people from Croatia (refugees) had come back. No numbers were given."

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kypr. I would now like to ask you something about the document that was tendered yesterday as Exhibit 312. That's tab 17. We'll just wait until we can see it on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: This is Exhibit 312, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, that is what I said, Exhibit 312.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kypr, can you please tell us if this report was drafted during the peace conference held in The Hague.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Now we have it.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, this document, as I can see quickly, there is no any reference concerning the -- even you have mentioned. And I have no any information about the situation, conferences in those days, because I have plenty of work on the spot, so I can't follow those events. And even it was a question for the head of mission or people from European Community. I was only a part of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Did you find out later, after the completion of your mission, that The Hague peace conference was held in early November 1991?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I don't remember. Because after my mission I have to prepare myself for another mission, and it was really very demanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kypr. Can you please tell me if you personally took part in the drafting of this report. And if yes, what was your part in the drafting of the report?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember, really. What I feel is that I had no time to -- to -- to speak with those people who came, at least -- at all, or I have a very limited time for them, so they were speaking more with -- with other people, probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: And the little time that you had at your disposal, did you find out, since the investigation was balanced, as claimed in the document, were there interviews with the Serb people who were in Ilok and did the Croats who returned to Ilok also talk about, were they asked about the situation?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... from lawyers and other experts, and they kept their information from -- for themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: So this was a special, a separate team, so you did not take part in the gathering of this information. Did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... made in -- or built in Zagreb headquarters, and as you can see in the report, they were working on many places, not only in Ilok. And as I told you, I don't remember about my cooperation with the team. I was not a part of the team, a member of the team.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kypr.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, maybe it's time for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. We'll adjourn now, resuming at five past 4.00. I hope you will be able to finish by the end of the next session, Mr. Vasic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Vasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kypr, to go back to the document that we were talking about before we took our break, can you please tell me, do you remember if the observer team had their conversation with you in the period that the report was being drafted; and what did you talk about, if you did talk?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... told you what I remember, but not very firmly, that I had no many time -- much time for that. But I -- I cannot say if it was at all or -- or how long it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Do you remember, if you remember, whether you talked about the topics mentioned in the report, or are you perhaps not able to remember?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... discussion, so I can't remember even the subject.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please tell me if you remember whether, during the implementation of your mission, you ever heard from people in the field, from officers, about any actions to resettle or move out the Croatian population? Do you recall anything like that?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you can repeat the question, because it -- there is in English text that I have heard from people in the field, from officers. I do remember the discussion with the local administrative chief of Lovas, and he has mentioned that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: What about the JNA officers?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... the administrative chief means in quotation marks, because he established himself, or he was elected locally in wartime.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is clear to me, but you didn't ever hear anything like this from JNA officers, that's what my question was, this local administrative chief in Lovas, you told us that already.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Today I -- I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please look at this document. Can you tell us if you know who sent this report from Zagreb. The document was sent from Zagreb, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: And do you know what this abbreviation means on this document, C-O-R-E-U, at the end of the text?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I already explained it. It is European Community at that time, or European Union, information for other countries and especially for so-called European correspondent, which is a special person from each country.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Do you know if this document was used in the adoption of political decisions by the Council of Europe or any other political bodies of the European Community?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: We - means Czechoslovakia - were no in that time a member of European Union, or European Community. So I have no any information concerning that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether a draft of this report was sent to the Belgrade regional centre before a final version was drafted, in order to have their opinion of the text?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell me -- can you please repeat your answer.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me if you remember whether you found a copy of this document; and if so, where, or was the copy found by the Prosecution investigator?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: According the symbols there, it is a copy, but this copy probably is -- comes from original, because there is written hand, "Comment, please." But I don't know if "P" is me, as -- as Petr, or if it means a separate ambassador, I really don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. It is clear to me. Do you remember whether you found this document or not?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It belongs to -- to the file I copied in -- in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us then whether there are any notes on which -- on the basis of which this report was compiled?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I told you, it -- this team was very independent, and I was not a member of the team, so I don't know the methods, procedures, and other information about the work.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Yesterday you responded to my learned colleague's question by reading aloud the contents of this document. I'm interested in the following: Did you ever personally, in the field, see the scenario described in items 1 through to 6, as interpreted, as described?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. Point 1: "Tensions, confusion and fear is built up by military presence in the vicinity of the villages and by provocative behaviour, controls, shootings." As concerns that, I believe that the tension or the fear which was felt by the -- those inhabitants of Ilok was there, because in the neighbourhood there were many clashes, shelling. A lot of refugees came from those villages to -- to Ilok. So they have brought the information. So if you wish to have an example, I believe that it could be this one. Next there is -- point 2: "Next, there is artillery and mortar shelling for several days. This shelling is mostly aimed at the Croatian part of the village. In this stage the churches are often hit and destroyed." I don't remember that I was a witness of such a case. 3: "Nearly all of the cases JNA ultimata are issued, demanding the collection and delivery of all weapons." I remember, probably in my notebook, that there is all mentioned. So I believe that it's one of examples that all weapons should be. But on the other hand, I remember that in negotiation about Ilok evacuation, there was a possibility I -- I -- I believe, for some people from local police to keep some small weaponry, only to -- to -- to cover an order in the village or in the city. Sorry, I am going through the text to find what do you want.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Item 4 is next: "With or without the results of the ultimatum issued, a military attack with tanks and infantry is carried out." Did you ever see such a thing, as an observer?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: To be correct, we were not on the spot, usually, where the action was there, because we were prohibited to go there because of our safety, and it was told from local authorities, it doesn't matter if it is JNA or Croatian side. And it was by our book, by our guidelines that we have -- we mustn't go there where our security is in a threat.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Did you know that the army remained inactive in such instances when the weapons had been turned over; for example, in Ilok?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I don't know other cases. May I repeat? In Ilok not, but I don't know other cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you for your assistance. I now wish to move to another topic, and that is Vukovar. Could we please see Exhibit 316 on the screen. That's tab 21.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Your Honour, could I just ask for clarification? I think my learned friend did ask in relation to this document, there are six heads, and I think that the witness was asked whether he had witnessed personally, or was aware of his perception of those six heads. As far as I can see, it has only got to four, but I don't know whether, in actual fact, the other two, namely five and six, are subsumed within the answer, where he says, "I don't another other cases." Now, I don't know if my learned friend is going to go on with five and six, but just for my own record, and perhaps the transcript may be clarified.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can ask the witness about items 5 and 6 in any case. But the problem I have is that we no longer have the document on the screen. But I would kindly ask the witness to go through his own papers. Since this concerns a sequence of events, the witness said he was not familiar with the events concerning some of the items, hence I found it unnecessary to continue with my line of questioning.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Point number 5 on the second page of the document: "At the same time or shortly after the attack, Chetniks entered the village to 'finish the job.' Accounts vary then from murder, killing, burning, looting and discrimination. Most of all elderly people who were not able to flee are involved." This concerns killing and burning. I believe that it's in the case of Lovas, because we saw there many burned houses and we got a list of, I don't know how many, 20 plus people who were killed. But I saw, even -- even in other villages burned houses, but I can't say who or what had happened, because it was afterwards when I came there and there were no witnesses, at least which were able to -- to testify or to say something, because people on the front line, they are afraiding all the time what do we wish to -- to hear. It's -- they are afraiding of everybody, even -- even of our mission, and it takes time to explain them what we are, and so it was a problem. And number 6: "Ilok was not destroyed. As such it represents an asset with a functional value and served a showcase to the monitor team." Yes, I believe that we did our best and we sent them unbelievable number of teams. It was not before -- I don't remember that we did it in -- in such a way. So -- so we tried to cover the situation and to help the people as much as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kypr.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: According the next paragraph, which is not numbered, the JNA systematically denied any guilt referring to the armament of the preparation and the provocative behaviour from their side."

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kypr, we're interested in the six items to establish whether a pattern existed. The next paragraph does not form a part of any of the items, therefore we can stop with your answer here.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... asked me about things which were mentioned in the document, not about paragraphs only. So it's why I am trying to answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. To move to Vukovar, I would kindly ask for Exhibit 316 to be displayed. Thank you. Sir, please take a look at the first page with number 0381398. Would you agree with me if I said that, as participants to the negotiations on the 19th of November, 1995, there are Mr. Cunningham, Mr. Brodin, Mr. Kypr, Mr. Reuters [phoen], Mr. Schou, and Mr. Henk van der Gaag as the representatives of the mission, as well as Colonel Pavkovic and Colonel Loncar, Colonel Memisevic, and Major Saric, and you thought this was Major Zaric, and they represented the JNA. This is what can be found in this particular report.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but the names were others, if I do remember. For instance, the second name is Mr. Brodin, and Mr. Kanteres, if I do remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we please see Exhibit 320, please. Mr. Kypr, for your sake and convenience, this is tab 22. On page 00381431, does it read the following: That Mr. Cunningham, Kanteres, Schou and Kypr were members of the team on the 20th? And that contacts were Colonel Pavkovic, Colonel Ivezic, General Jerko Crmenic, Major Zeljko Koritnik?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, according names in the team, I can read that those are the names in the team. And those names down on the page only -- only number 4 you have mentioned, Major Zeljko Koritnik, I don't know if he is -- or he was a major. He was MUDR, means medicine doctor.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you be so kind as to take a look at your notes, page 046 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters apologise, we did not catch the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: 0468-7772. Sir, you have your notes before you, I believe. Could you tell us whether on this page, under Negoslavci, the 20th of November, you made an entry mentioning Colonel Pavkovic and whether the entire paragraph with three sentences had been put together with the name of Pavkovic?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: First question: Yes, I wrote it down. It's my hand. This -- the name of Colonel Pavkovic. As concerns if it is connected with the name, I don't know. Maybe.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Perhaps you don't know whether this has any connection to what I had in mind, but I wanted to know the following: Is this part of the document split in two parts, one pertaining to Pavkovic and the other one on page 0648-7772?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, 7773.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I am right, please, correct me if not. So between the sentence that, "3 JNA soldiers who were captured, were taken out from the hospital, they are in the Negoslavci hospital." And the abbreviation "Neg" means Negoslavci, and the date, the 20th of November, there is a line which means that the meeting or briefing in Negoslavci started from there -- from this line. So it is splitting those two text.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us where the next line appears in your text; after which sentence?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is after -- "General Raseta," are the last two words of the sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Therefore, the part between the two lines should form a singular context, or rather, the same conversation, if I'm not mistaken?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I presume Colonel Pavkovic was introduced to you, or rather, he had to introduce himself before seeing you on the first time -- for the first time on the 19th of November. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't remember, because we have met so many people on the front line in -- of various ranks and various capacities, so it was hundreds of people.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: But your liaison officers who were there with you knew Colonel Nebojsa Pavkovic and I presume they confirmed to you that he was indeed the person, and perhaps they were the ones who put this name in your notebook?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... because it was written by my hand, so I was told that it -- in that case it is -- it is Colonel Pavkovic. But we haven't checked those names, and my notebook even was only a part of the business. So other monitors were taking their notes and I was following more the -- the subject, because I was working in both languages, and they can follow the form, so persons and behaviour and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: And when you were drafting the report, I believe you compared your notes and those of the other members of the mission, such as Mr. Cunningham and the rest, and then you compiled the report as a team report?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was usual procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we please see document 0D00-0219 in the original on the screen? And the English translation, 0D00-0221. This is a report of the Monitoring Commission dated the 19th of November, 1991. Could we see the second page, please. Thank you. On the second page we can read the following: "The group that visited Vukovar spoke with Colonel Nebojsa Pavkovic, and was briefed in detail on the evacuation of the wounded. Colonel Pavkovic used solid arguments and in a convincing way removed any shadow of doubt on the part of the monitors as to the ability of the members of the JNA to organise and implement the agreed evacuation of those wounded in a fair way. Colonel Pavkovic's talks with the monitors dealt with the treatment of wounded members of Croatian paramilitary formations. The monitors were told that they would be treated as prisoners of war and that their names would be given to the Red Cross." Sir, we can see in this report that on the 19th of November you met with Colonel Pavkovic, and we can also see what the topic of discussion was. Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I see the first page?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have the first page on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because you have mentioned the 19th, and the -- the next text on the -- on the second page is speaking about the 18th, so I'm surprised that -- the date 19th is before the 18th. So only -- only it's why I am asking. Can you -- can you move the text further, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: If you take a look at the heading, you will see that the date mentioned is the 19th of November, 1991. And in your report the discussion mentioned is that on the 19th of November at 2.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I can only say that the text is -- is done by the -- from JNA side, so it's the explanation on -- or presentation like it was presented by -- by the JNA or -- or as MOD, if you wish. According my remarks from the 19th, and you have the translation of my remarks, so it's all I can do, or maybe there is some report from the team. So there is the statement of European Union Monitoring Mission, and there is a part of -- of my remarks concerning that -- that date. So it's what I have noticed and what I do -- not remember, but what I -- what I wrote. I -- I remember that as -- as generally, not the -- the -- that the sentence is such as is written in the book. But I feel that -- that there was a long discussion about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we tender this document as an exhibit, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Could I make application that it be marked for identification?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Vasic, it will be received for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, this will be marked for identification, 330.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I would just like to know the reason for my learned friend's request. Is it the authenticity or the content of the document that prompted this request?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Moore.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Yes, I will. Firstly, the witness indicates an element of surprise about the continuity of the particulars, and when one reads the document, it seems that the European -- or the ECMM mission members apparently were looking at the quality and quantity of combat equipment that had arrived, that they would inspect newly arrived armoured equipment -- perhaps if I just go through the various parts. On the first page, two, third paragraph, there is reference to the group spending the night at Ovcara. Then turning the page, the third paragraph -- or the second again refers to Ovcara, there is the fact that Monitor Mission members were sent a telex referring to the time and quantity of combat equipment that arrived. And then the penultimate paragraph there seems to be some suggestion about a political evaluation. I'm not sure exactly to what that relates. And then finally it's been agreed that in keeping with the agreement in the understanding, the Monitor Mission will inspect the newly arrived armoured equipment of the 1st Brigade at 10.00 in the morning on the 20th of November, a time when it seems to be that the ECMM are supposed to be at the bridge and on the way to the hospital. And my understanding, from the evidence in chief, that the scope of the monitoring mission was to basically merely monitor and do nothing else. That is why I asked for it to be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. So the content, in very large part, is questioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Even though this second part really does not have much to do with the Monitoring Mission, but very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: May I just deal with one matter, and I should have said it. If my learned friend has an original document which he has access to and I can see, it may well be that I can assist him.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I can discuss this later with my learned friend. We do have the documents with stamps, so I hope that we will resolve this issue. Could we now please have Exhibit 316 on the monitor, please. Page -- it's page 2, 00381399. The next page is marked 00381399. Could we please zoom in on the page. Thank you. The first two-thirds of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kypr, you have that in tab 21. Can you please read what it says in paragraph (d), items (1), (2) and (3). What did Colonel Pavkovic say about why prisoners of war would not be permitted to leave with the convoy? So could you please read items (1), (2) and (3).

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Second sentence: "Colonel Pavkovic stated that prisoners of war would not be allowed to depart, as: "(1) the prisoners of war are under JNA control. "(2) if he did --" or they did; I don't understand the abbreviation -- "Serb irregulars/local citizens would attack the convoy. "(3) the prisoners of war would be exchanged for JNA prisoners of war at some future time."

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kypr. Could you please take your diary now and look at page 0468-7763. Have you found it, this typed part? And there you can see Vidic's proposals unclear in the English, after that it says, "Prisoners of war from the National Guard and MUP will be exchanged for our prisoners." Do you remember whether this was one of the proposals that Marin Vidic stated in the negotiations?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, the sentence is in original written in English, "Prisoners of war from NG --" means National Guard Croatian, and "MUP" means Croatian police -- "will be changed with our prisoners of war." So it means with our prisoners of war, so I understand that it is told by the side of -- from the side of JNA. "Our prisoners of war." Because the first part of the sentence is speaking that prisoners of war from NGO -- sorry, NG and MUP. So it was told by -- by JNA, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: What about Mr. Vidic's proposals? Do you remember anything about that? Because I can see that it's just a line above this one.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, sir, those remarks are only part of the whole discussion. So it is not word-by-word if it is not important -- if I didn't feel that it is important.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we go back to the page that is on the screen now, and can we look at the bottom of the page. We're looking at the second part of the page, paragraph 2. Mr. Kypr, do you see paragraph 2 on this page, which begins with the words, "Involvement with the Red Cross." What I'm interested in is does it state in the text, in the last two sentences of this paragraph, "Paragraph 4 of the fax message is missing." Is that what it says?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, sir, I -- it's really difficult to read Cunningham's handwriting. If some of native English speakers there can -- can help us with -- to read the original text from -- from the original copy, because otherwise I -- I -- I can read the last sentence. It is, "Four Red Cross teams will monitor move of refugees and hospital evacuation." But the previous sentence is really difficult, at the end of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I can read to you what it says in the -- in translation, which we received on page 03030939, and it says there: "Paragraph 6 of the fax message is missing. Four teams of the RCB monitor the transfer of refugees and the evacuation of the hospital." Does this perhaps refresh your memory?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... the "Involvement with Red Cross was very limited and I am not certain what agreements they have made --" probably about writing list of wounded persons -- "to be moved or if them have determined and agreed --" and I -- it's illegible for me, those abbreviations. "The neutrality --" I don't know what does it mean. "Paragraph 6 --"

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: I wonder if "PD" might mean "period." It's only a suggestion.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After words of fax paragraph message, there is a full stop. And next sentence starts with number "four" written, and then there is the figure "4."

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: But we don't know what this abbreviation means, "IAW."

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. Could we now shortly just go back to your notebook, page number 0648-7774.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: 7774, but this is on the next page, because this number actually covers two pages of the typed text. Where it says, "8.30 the colonel spoke with the commander of the exchange zone." We're talking about Colonel Pavkovic here, is that correct? And was this on the 20th of November, 1991?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether -- please, could you repeat your answer.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether the commander of the exchange zone was the chief of the staff of the 1st Military District, Colonel Vladimir Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we now have document 0D00-0223 on the monitor. That's the English -- actually, the English version is 0D00-25 [as interpreted] dated the 20th of November 1991. Again, it's a report of the commission for monitoring the activities of the Monitoring Mission. Can we focus on the bottom part of the page, please. Thank you. Paragraph 2, monitor mission activities, it states: "The EC Monitoring Mission today continued to monitor the evacuation activities of the wounded from the Vukovar Hospital and refugees or the Croatian people from Vukovar. A group of six monitors (three teams), was received in the village of Negoslavci by Colonel Pavkovic, who informed them about the way the location was organised. One of the teams was sent to Ovcara to join a team of monitors who had spent the night there in order to monitor the evacuation of refugees towards Croatia, as agreed between the units of the JNA and the Croatian staff. The second observer team observed the evacuation of the wounded from the Vukovar Hospital, while the third team remained in Negoslavci in order to coordinate activities." Is this something that took place on the 20th of November when your three teams came to monitor the evacuation in Vukovar and the evacuation of civilians who had spent the night at Ovcara and also to monitor the evacuation from the Vukovar Hospital? And did Colonel Pavkovic receive you on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I understand, there were many teams, and I don't remember in detail their tasks. But it is covered by the -- I believe that there are some documents which are covering that, as well as from Belgrade, as well as from Zagreb, but in that time I have no -- really no time to -- to follow all the situation. So what I can confirm, from this text, that one team exactly then we came there as four persons, but we split it -- or three persons, I don't know -- but we split it -- the team, and Dr. Schou and me, we stayed there to follow the -- the evacuation of Vukovar's hospital, and the rest, Cunningham and I don't know who else, have moved to -- I don't know, to organise the whole thing and to communicate with these other parts of ECMM.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Do you have information that the convoy that set out in the morning, the refugees and civilians' convoy that set off from Ovcara that previously spent night in Morovic and which left Ovcara in the direction of Vinkovci was fired upon by the Croatian side near Nustar? Are you aware of that? We have a report of that from a journalist.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- now I -- I am thinking about one of remarks in my notebook, and I -- I am not sure if it is the -- the reaction, but there somebody from JNA, or in the name of MOD is complaining that Croatian side and -- but the sentence is not -- is not clear, but maybe it is connected there, so it's -- it's what we were told. I cannot say because I was not on the spot, I didn't see anything which was -- which was connected with this case. So what is written in my notebook is only what -- what we were told.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kypr.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to tender this document as an exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: I again would wish to have the document marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Similar position as for the last?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Yes. There is no evidence that any European monitor was ever sent to Ovcara and I would wish the matter to be clarified with regard to original documentation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document will be marked for identification with the reference number 331.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I hope to resolve this with my learned friend, although there is a report that the observer mission did monitor the convoy from Ovcara that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Anyway, Mr. Kypr, for a moment I would like to discuss something that you mentioned about your entry to the hospital, and you told my learned friend about it, including information that some prisoners of war had been taken out of the hospital. Can you please tell me, who told you that, and when and what were the circumstances in which you were told, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember who told it, but I remember that it was the -- the first intention when we went into the hospital to find the -- the manager of the hospital, which was Dr. Bosanac, according our knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: And when you asked about Mrs. Bosanac, who did you ask about her; was it anybody from the staff or did you ask a patient? Who told you that some people were taken away? Was it hospital staff, and where did they tell you that, which part of the hospital?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. There was dark in the cellar, and it was really very dramatic situation, so I don't remember persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And after that, you informed the liaison officer, I assumed it was Colonel Memisevic, about the fact that some people were taken out of the hospital. He was your liaison officer who escorted you, he was appointed by the SSNO.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... from our team. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: You don't remember who it was. Did anybody from your team inform your liaison officer?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose so, because I -- I remember that some -- in some remarks or -- it is mentioned, but now it's 16 years, so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: In response to a question by my learned friend yesterday, you told us that after about an hour spent at the hospital, Colonel Cunningham went to Belgrade to do something, to resolve the situation with the prisoners of war who had been taken away from the hospital. Do you know where he went in Belgrade; who did he go to?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I remember, I said that Cunningham went to take care about other convoy, plus to inform about that. And I -- I have to stress that I am not sure about exact timing. So it could be half an hour or one hour. I really don't know in those circumstances.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: I would like to know whether Mr. Cunningham told you where he went in Belgrade, who did he go to see?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your answer.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry. No, he was a chief of monitors, and he was responsible for those things.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. To one of my yesterday's questions you replied that you saw General Zivota Panic on several occasions. He was the then-commander of the 1st Army region, and a part of his area of responsibility included Vukovar; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember a few meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Yesterday you also said that immediately after your return to Vukovar you attended a meeting with the representatives of the press and they took your photographs there.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the exact sentence, but I am not quite sure if there were journalists. But I saw the footage of this meeting on Serb TV afterwards. I know that there was a military reporter following those events each time. I believe so, each time. And only in this case, as I remember, the footage went -- went on TV.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we now please see document 0D00-0227 in the original, and its translation into English 0D00-0228. This is another report of the commission monitoring the Monitoring Mission activities, the date the 23rd of November, 1991. Could we please zoom in on the lower part of the page. Item 2, Monitor Mission activities. It states: "At our request, the First Military District commander, Lieutenant General Zivota Panic, today received the Belgrade-based European Monitor Mission members, headed by Mr. Petr Kypr with whom he had long and friendly talks." Mr. Kypr, I want to know whether, during these conversations, you told General Panic about your comments relating to the events at Vukovar Hospital. Did you familiarise him with the situation?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The reason why we were - and "we" means European Union Monitoring Mission -- were invited to headquarters, was that there was some inappropriate behaviour of one of our teams. We had no evidence on that except we got information from the other side and we have to check it, so it was not sure what -- what will be our answer to that. I believe that it's why it was me and Colonel Cunningham, or I don't know who else, but I believe that it was Colonel Cunningham, because he is responsible for the work of monitors. So he is responsible to answer that. So it was the -- the case we went there, and it -- it was why Ambassador Perrin was not there, because we went there only in this particular case of violence of some -- something. Which, afterwards, we saw that it's -- it's not true, at least as I remember those allegations.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: During the conversation did you discuss the conduct in Vukovar? That -- that was the topic, and whether the behaviour occurred in Vukovar, and as I believe at the end it was established that it wasn't.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... this allegation was concerning one of our team, or one of our monitors during their way with this convoy, but I am not sure if it is convoy from Vukovar or from other cases -- or from other places, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You explained why you were invited, but I'm interested in the -- I'm not so interested in the detail as to the actual conduct of the Monitoring Mission, but I wanted to know whether you told General Panic what you had to say in relation to the evacuation from Vukovar Hospital and that the POWs were taken away.
